Bill overview page listing her co-sponsorship of the same single-subject ESA bill, which the Governor signed as Chapter 388.

passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding section 15-2401, beginning in the 2022-2023 school year, in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, "qualified student" includes a resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state in any of the following: ( a ) A preschool program for children with disabilities. ( b ) A kindergarten program. ( c ) Any of grades one through twelve. 2. Does not otherwise qualify for an Arizona empowerment scholarship account pursuant to this chapter.
passages.note: Chaptered text of the bill she co-sponsored and voted for; the added section 15-2401.01 makes every student eligible to enroll in an Arizona public school a qualified student.

rows.reasoning: Martinez co-sponsored HB 2853 (2022) and voted Y on its House Third Reading; the single-subject bill's added section 15-2401.01 makes any resident "eligible to enroll in a public school in this state" a qualified student for an empowerment scholarship account, and section 15-2402 pays the account "an amount that is equivalent to ninety percent of the sum of the base support level and additional assistance" that would otherwise go to the student's district, spendable on "Tuition or fees at a qualified school" — a nongovernmental school, with no exclusion of religious schools. That is the rung "Providing universal vouchers so that education funding follows the student to any school — public, private, or religious — chosen by the family", not the next rung down, because eligibility reaches every public-school-eligible student rather than "most families, not all". The acts fall within her 2021-11-01 to 2023-01-09 term in this same chamber, so they are in-term.
